Boston’s Emerald Necklace was the vision of Frederick Olmsted, the same architect who designed Central Park and the US Capital Gardens. The vision was to have a seamless park connection all the way from the Boston Common to Jamaica Pond. Today, it features a the green line riding through the sunken garden, bike paths for commuters, and running routes. It’s a massively important bike network connection for cyclists, however for anyone who has been on the Necklace, knows that the connections and intersections are just horribly designed, and Fenway itself is a complete mess of high speed roads and turns and unsafe crosswalks. There’s a lot of work that needs to be done to make this beautiful park, well integrated in Boston’s pedestrian and bike network to make this accessible and useful. #citybiking #boston #cafebiking #fredericklawolmsted

This pretty much sums up Boston’s horrible street infrastructure. Biking on Commonwealth Ave is just a fight between trucks, cars, students walking, and professors biking. The delivery driver doesn’t have a designated safe parking spot to unload so he stops in the middle of the road and bike lane, opening the door into the bike lane and blocking the woman on a bike. If she tries to go around the car then she’ll get hit by a truck that probably doesn’t even see her in time because of how high up the truck driver is. @bostonu let’s get some temporary barriers out and designated delivery and rideshare drop offs? I know yall are waiting for the @cityofboston and @bosstreetscabinet to update their infrastructure, but that’s gonna take about 10 years. Would appreciate some small cones or an BU officer to be Comm Ave at key intersections!!

Somerville Community Path looks surreal right now. The path extends from Davis Square all the way to the Boston, making the bike ride completely car free and safe ❤️ @somervillecity has made so many upgrades to their sustainable infrastructure and this is bike-highway is really just the cherry on top of a wonderful growing street network. #citybiking #somerville

If there one thing cyclists of all kinds know how to do…it’s finish a ride at a cafe. We ride to the best cafes in the Boston area every single weekend, and we change the meeting point every ride. Join a ride that starts in your neighborhood :) #citybiking #boston #cafebiking

After the city cafe ride, gotta pay tribute to the amazing regional network of trails that the Boston area has :) The minuteman trail and reformatory branch trail are an incredible way to see the fall colors this year 🍁🍁🍁 Stop at @myhautecoffee in Concord for a post-ride pastries :)
